description: Traceability tests. Every number in the model must be reachable from GEOMETRY-CONTROL.md, every source cited there must exist in SOURCE-REGISTER.md, and no dimension from a neighbouring East River bridge may appear anywhere. Run with: python scripts/validate_dimensions.py

tests.title: Every source cited by a control exists in the source register
Every control graded A, B or C cites at least one source
tests.rationale: Only grade D may be sourceless. Enforced in the parser as well; asserted here so a parser regression is visible.

tests.title: Every placeholder control cites no source
tests.rationale: A placeholder must not appear to rest on evidence.

tests.title: Every control reference on a part resolves to a control ID
No Manhattan Bridge dimension appears as a control value
tests.rationale: This repository's brief was adapted from the Manhattan Bridge, so cross-contamination is a structural risk rather than a hypothetical one. Checked as values in the declared unit, because the failure mode is a plausible number arriving without a label.

tests.title: No Williamsburg Bridge dimension appears as a control value
tests.rationale: Haight and Patel give the Williamsburg stiffening truss as 67 ft wide and about 40 ft deep. On its first run this test failed on a 40 ft placeholder truss offset of this repository's own; the placeholder was moved rather than exempted, because an arbitrary value that happens to look like a forbidden one blunts the guard.

tests.title: The brief carries no control rows of its own
tests.rationale: GEOMETRY-CONTROL.md is the only authority for a dimension. Two documents carrying CTL- rows is how a model drifts.

tests.title: No part models a rail line of any kind
tests.rationale: The adapted brief asks for four subway tracks. The Brooklyn Bridge carries no rail lines: not the Manhattan Bridge's subway, and not its own elevated and trolley tracks, which were removed in the mid-twentieth century. See OQ-012.

tests.title: Every open question cited by a part exists in GEOMETRY-CONTROL.md section 5
Every part declares a non-empty source_basis
No part claims a photogrammetry or survey basis in Milestone 1
tests.rationale: No such source has been ingested. Any such basis would silently promote a part to MEASURED.

tests.title: Every part carries the full required metadata block
Sources cited by controls have been read, not merely registered
tests.rationale: A source in the verification queue may be named in prose but may not carry a control. This is what stops a citation from being aspirational.

tests.title: Structural elements the sources count must actually be modelled
tests.rationale: A reviewer noticed the cables appearing to attach below the tower tops. The elevation was right; the cause was that CTL-046 -- eight cast iron saddle bearings, grade A -- was registered and never built, so nothing showed where the cable went. A sourced count with no geometry is a silent hole in the model, and this test closes that class.

tests.title: Census of sourced controls that carry no geometry
tests.rationale: Report-only: many controls are recorded purely for traceability and must NOT reach geometry, such as the superseded tower height CTL-021. But this census is how the missing saddles were found, so it stays visible.

tests.title: An unreviewed photograph corpus grades nothing
tests.rationale: SRC-018 is harvested, licence-checked and entirely auto_screened: 272 photographs nobody has looked at. The register row exists and looks complete, which makes citing it by accident easy. This fails the build if any control or material rule cites it before a person has accepted a single photograph. It is also the guard that lets the corpus be committed early -- the evidence can sit in the repository without silently becoming evidence.

tests.title: A photograph with no camera position says so out loud
tests.rationale: 193 of the 272 records are archival or uploaded without EXIF and legitimately have no camera fix. The shared contract permits the omission only when position_source is 'unknown', so that a genuinely position-less archive plate cannot be confused with a survey that silently dropped its GPS. This asserts the distinction locally rather than trusting that whatever wrote the file got it right.

tests.title: Stated date precision never exceeds what the timestamp carries
tests.rationale: The first harvest truncated free text to ten characters and stamped every record 'day', so the corpus read captured_at 'Taken on 2' with a confident day-precision badge on it. Nothing caught it, because every test asked whether the model was sourced and none asked whether the sources were sane. A wrong date that announces itself is recoverable; a wrong date wearing a precision badge is not.

tests.title: A photograph may grade a material but never a dimension
tests.rationale: SRC-018 is now reviewed, so it may legitimately be cited - and the moment a source becomes citable is the moment its limits stop being theoretical. A photograph settles what something is made of and how it is arranged; without scale control in the frame it cannot measure. This allows SRC-018 on material rules and forbids it on any dimensional control, so the 85 ft deck and the 1595.5 ft span cannot quietly acquire a photographic justification.

tests.title: A claim about today's fabric may not rest on an archival photograph
tests.rationale: The accepted corpus spans 1867 to 2026. MAT-009 says the roadway is asphalt and MAT-010 says the promenade is timber -- both present-tense claims about surfaces that are renewed on a maintenance cycle, and neither was true of the 1883 bridge. The reviewer avoided the trap by instinct, tagging all 19 pre-1960 photographs `context` and nothing else, but nothing enforced it: one archival frame tagged `deck` would have made MAT-009 rest partly on a surface that no longer exists. Categories are now declared `renewed` or `stable` in the campaign, and a renewed subject may only be evidenced by photography after the stated cutoff. Granite is stable and an 1876 photograph of it is still evidence; asphalt is not.
